design_notes.balance_rule: every scam/legit pair shares the same signals vector
design_notes.removed: all 'no credentials needed' / 'no password is needed' disclaimers (they leaked personal_info_req)

examples.text: Dear Customer, we noticed a login from a new device on your account. If this wasn't you, confirm your identity at example-bank.info/secure to restore access.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Lookalike domain and identity confirmation that captures credentials; 'restore access' pressures action.

examples.text: Hello user, we noticed a login from a new device on your account. If this wasn't you, confirm your identity in the app under Security to restore access.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Genuine sign-in notice that asks the user to confirm identity inside the authenticated app's Security tab, not via a message link.

examples.text: Urgent: your account will be limited in 24 hours unless you confirm your details. Complete verification at example-bank.info/verify. Action required to keep access.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Artificial deadline plus a verification link on a lookalike domain; 'action required' and 'limited in 24 hours' are pressure tactics.

examples.text: Urgent: your account will be limited in 24 hours unless you confirm your details. Complete verification in your online banking profile. Action required to keep access.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Scheduled verification reminder with identical urgency language; the action completes in the authenticated profile, not a message link.

examples.text: Hello user, I'm from the ExampleBank account team. We're updating our records. Could you reply with your online banking username and password so we can verify your profile?
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Subtle scam: no link, no urgency, no money — a conversational records-update request asking the recipient to reply with credentials.

examples.text: Hello user, I'm from the ExampleBank account team. We're updating our records. Could you confirm your contact details in your online banking profile under Settings?
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Legitimate records-update request using the same phrase pattern; the confirmation happens in the authenticated Settings page.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a transfer of $480.00 to an unrecognized payee is pending. Cancel it at example-bank.info/cancel immediately to prevent loss.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Fabricated pending transfer plus a lookalike cancel link; 'prevent loss' pressures a click without asking for credentials.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a transfer of $480.00 to payee ACME-LLC is pending. Cancel it in your online banking under Transfers if unrecognized.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Real transfer notice naming the payee; cancellation happens in the authenticated Transfers view.

examples.text: Urgent: your debit card is frozen. Unfreeze it now at example-bank.info/unfreeze by entering your card number and PIN. A replacement card fee may apply if not unfrozen.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Fake freeze plus a card-number-and-PIN request on a lookalike domain; the fee threat adds pressure.

examples.text: Urgent: your debit card is frozen due to a security hold. Unfreeze it in the app under Cards by re-authenticating. A replacement card fee may apply if not unfrozen.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Legitimate unfreeze instruction using the same urgency; re-authentication happens inside the app's Cards section.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a new payee 'Global Transfer Co' was added to your account. If this wasn't you, call 1-555-0100 or visit example-bank.info/payees. Our fraud team is available 24/7.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Fabricated payee addition with a fictional callback and lookalike link; '24/7 fraud team' is borrowed legitimacy.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a new payee 'Global Transfer Co' was added to your account. If this wasn't you, call 1-555-0100 or review payees in your online banking. Our fraud team is available 24/7.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Legitimate payee-change notice with verified contact; review happens in the authenticated payees view.

examples.text: Hello user, this is the ExampleBank security team. We blocked a suspicious login. To restore access, reply with your password so we can verify it's really you.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Subtle scam: conversational verification pretext asking the recipient to reply with a password.

examples.text: Hello user, this is the ExampleBank security team. We blocked a suspicious login. To restore access, re-authenticate in the app under Security so we can verify it's really you.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Legitimate reset guidance using the same verification phrase; re-authentication happens in the app's Security section.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a $12.99 monthly service fee was charged to your account. View the breakdown and dispute it at example-bank.info/fees. Upgrade to premium to waive fees.
examples.label: scam
examples.rationale: Fabricated fee plus a dispute link on a lookalike domain; the premium upsell is a distractor.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a $12.99 monthly service fee was charged to your account. View the breakdown and dispute it in the app under Billing. Upgrade to premium to waive fees.
examples.label: legit
examples.rationale: Standard billing notice to the real domain; dispute completes in the authenticated Billing view.

examples.text: Hello user, your statement for May is ready. Review it at example-bank.info/statements and confirm your account number to download.

examples.rationale: Statement notice with an account-number confirmation on a lookalike domain.

examples.text: Hello user, your statement for May is ready. Review it in the app under Statements by confirming your account number there.

examples.text: Dear Customer, a $250.00 refund was processed to your account. Claim it in the app under Refunds by confirming your SSN and account details there.

examples.rationale: Legitimate refund confirmation using the same identity-confirmation phrase; it happens in the authenticated Refunds view.
